headline: Fire is not a thing—it's a process: rapid oxidation releasing heat and light
universal_truth: Transformation often looks like destruction, but it's really just change
fun_facts: Fire requires three things: fuel, oxygen, and heat—remove any one and fire dies
Humans have controlled fire for at least 400,000 years—it shaped our evolution
A candle flame contains millions of tiny diamond particles forming and burning instantly
discussion_questions: What in your life needs to 'burn away' for new growth?
How has the discovery of fire shaped what it means to be human?
What's something you've seen transform that seemed like destruction at first?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Look at a flame. It dances, it flickers, it seems alive. But fire isn't a thing at all—it's a process. What you see is a chemical reaction made visible: matter transforming, releasing ancient sunlight stored in fuel. Fire is transformation you can see.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Fire seems to appear from nowhere and disappear just as mysteriously. You can't hold it. It has no mass. So what is fire, exactly? It's not solid, liquid, or gas in the traditional sense. What are we actually looking at?
cliff.prompt: What is fire at its most basic?

options.text: A visible chemical reaction where fuel rapidly combines with oxygen
options.response: Exactly. Fire is combustion—the rapid oxidation of fuel releasing heat and light.

options.text: A type of plasma or energy field
options.response: Flames can contain plasma at high temperatures, but the core process is simpler...

q1.title: The Fire Triangle
q1.script: Fire needs three things: fuel to burn, oxygen to react with, and heat to start the reaction. This is called the fire triangle. Remove any one element and fire dies. This is why smothering flames works—you're removing oxygen.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Fire Triangle"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Human Fire
q2.script: Humans have controlled fire for at least 400,000 years. Fire let us cook food—making more nutrients available, possibly enabling our large brains. Fire gave us warmth, protection, and community. Fire made us human.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Diamonds in Flames
q3.script: In the hottest part of a candle flame, soot particles are heated so intensely that they briefly form tiny diamond nanocrystals—then burn away in milliseconds. Every candle contains fleeting diamonds, appearing and vanishing faster than you can blink.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Fire reminds us that transformation can look like destruction. When things burn—in our lives, our relationships, our plans—something new is also being created. The ash contains seeds.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 36. Tomorrow, we'll explore why ice floats—a quirk of physics that makes life on Earth possible. Until then, if you see a flame, remember: you're watching matter transform before your eyes.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Transformation Reflection - What Needs to Burn
growTrack.activity: Think of something in your life that feels like it's ending or being destroyed—a habit, a belief, a phase. Instead of resisting, ask: what new thing might emerge from these ashes? Transformation requires release.
